alternatives_and_negative_results: Do not infer DSP/BRAM/CLB fit, Fmax or board behavior from Python or code inspection.
applicability: FPGA implementation and radar hardware delivery.
assessed_root_cause: Functional/numeric equivalence, HDL simulation, synthesis/resource mapping, timing closure and physical board behavior are different evidence levels.
author_role: historical project engineering record, backfilled by FPGA engineering copilot
chosen_corrective_method: Create synthesizable RTL, verify it against independent golden vectors, then separately run HDL simulation, ISE synthesis/implementation/STA and physical AX309 readback.
generalizable_lesson: Keep every verification claim scoped to the actual execution layer and tool evidence.
initial_faulty_assumption_or_design_deci: A software reference or bit-true Python qualification could be described as proof that the design fits or executes on the FPGA.
non_applicability: Does not invalidate the accepted Python reference or S04 deterministic numerical evidence within its scope.
observable_consequence: S01 and C02 explicitly exclude resource/timing proof; C06R2 explicitly records no RTL/synthesis/FPGA. The active host has no ISE, Vivado, Icarus, Verilator, GHDL or Yosys executable.
observed_problem: The project has extensive Python deterministic and statistical evidence, but no RTL, synthesis, STA or physical-board run is recorded.
repeatable_validation: Record tool versions, exact commands, logs, outputs, resource reports, timing paths and board measurements at their respective stages.
reviewer_role: documentary evidence validation by FPGA engineering copilot; not a separate human reviewer
safety_contract_constraints: No claim of synthesis, timing closure or hardware execution until actual tool and board evidence exists.
title: Software-reference PASS does not establish FPGA resource, timing or physical-board PASS
